newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sentrachem leaps on Dow buy offer.
newsitem.headline: Sentrachem leaps on Dow buy offer.

text.p: Shares in South African chemical firm Sentrachem Ltd soared in early trade after U.S. giant Dow Chemical Co said it had made an offer to buy the firm at 10.50 rand a share.
At 0750 GMT Sentrachem shares jumped nearly 27.0 percent or 213 cents to 10.05 rand -- its best level in nine months. Volumes, were, however tiny at only 3,000 shares.
"The share will move up to the offer level, but there is not much demand as people don't know how long it will take to settle the deal or if it will definitely go through," a dealer said.
Sentrachem shares were reinstated on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Tuesday after they were suspended on Monday pending a major announcement.
The Dow offer values Sentrachem, which undergoing a major restructure following a disastrous first half, at over two billion rand.

Dow, which disinvested from South Africa in the 1980s but returned to operate a chemicals plant in 1995, said it had already sealed an agreement from Sankorp Ltd -- which holds 38.74 percent of Sentrachem -- to accept and recommend the offer.

In the six months to end-February Sentrachem slumped to a pre-tax loss of 257 million rand on the back of one-off charges of 261 million rand from forward cover contracts and restructuring costs at unit Sanachem.
Dow is the world's fifth largest chemicals company with annual sales of more than $20 billion, about 40,000 employees and customers in 157 countries.
